text:
ashley-sales: Quick sync — Acme POC asking to run Redwood Private behind their on-prem proxy + PrivateLink. They want client IP preserved, mTLS to our endpoint, and a tight firewall allowlist. Pricing question: should we recommend NAT egress or PrivateLink with interface endpoints?

ben-arch: For client IP preservation + low egress complexity, PrivateLink (interface endpoint) is usually cleaner. It avoids NAT translation but needs per-AZ ENIs and egress bandwidth pricing.

nate-netops: FYI their firewall team will only accept a short list of IPs and a stable cert fingerprint. Can we provide stable egress IPs for Private deployments?

olivia-sre: For Private (customer-managed) we can offer static egress IPs if they pick Dedicated with an EIP/NAT or we can route via our egress NAT pool. Hosted PrivateLink via interface endpoints is per-region, not per-customer-IP stable unless we assign static EIPs.

ashley-sales: Pricing note for customer: they asked for cost delta — they expect a callout comparing NAT Gateway vs PrivateLink per-GB. Can we give rough ballpark?

ben-arch: Rough: NAT gateway (cloud provider) -> data transfer + NAT hourly; PrivateLink -> charges for endpoint hours + data processed. For heavy egress (>5 TB/mo) PrivateLink + dedicated EIPs typically wins on latency but depends on provider pricing. I can draft numbers if you want.

ashley-sales: Yes please. Also security Q: they insist on mTLS to our ingestion endpoint and KMS integration for keys. Is there anything blocking?

sara-security: mTLS support is fine on our Private endpoints. For customer-managed key material we support KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments but we need their key policy and rotation window. Also we'll need answers on logging retention for audit.

nate-netops: Firewall rules they need: allow outbound to our region IPs on 443 only, allow SNI preserved. They also asked for SNAT preservation for source IP — is that possible with interface endpoint?

ben-arch: Interface endpoints terminate inside customer's VPC so source IP is preserved when traffic goes to their private proxy, but if the proxy then egresses to us via NAT, source IP may change. For full preservation, customer can route directly to our endpoint inside their VPC or use a transparent TCP tunnel.

olivia-sre: Quick config snippet they can hand to firewall team:

```
# Allowlist example (customer side)
# Allow outbound TCP 443 to the following IP ranges (example):
203.0.113.10/32  # redwood-ingest-1 (us-west-2)
203.0.113.11/32  # redwood-ingest-2 (us-west-2)
# TLS SNI: *.redwood-inference.internal
# mTLS: client cert CN must match: Acme-POC-client
```

sara-security: Also add: they must support TLS 1.2+ and ciphers AES_GCM; we will require client cert rotation every 90 days for the POC. Provide their SOC/ISO contact for questionnaire.

ashley-sales: Action items for us: (1) ben to draft cost comparison quicksheet, (2) olivia to provide egress IP list and sample firewall rules, (3) sara to list KMS/key-policy items and required questionnaire answers — target EOD tomorrow. I'll coordinate with Acme's security.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: private endpoint template version v2.4 will include mTLS config flag `enable_client_cert: true` — ops ticket 3782 created.

nate-netops: Thanks — looping in Acme firewall lead now.

ashley-sales: Thanks team :pray: — I'll post the results back to the customer and book a call if they want to review configs live.
